text:
Sampled HR@10 measures ranking within its candidate distribution; it is not a calibrated estimate of full-catalog HR@10. [Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) show sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation. [RecSys 2025 research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05398) separates sampling reliability into resolution, fidelity, robustness to exposure bias, and agreement with ground-truth preferences; candidate composition matters alongside sample size. A [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) investigates performance and popularity bias across random, popularity-based, in-batch, and adaptive training negatives. Training-sampler findings do not establish which evaluation sampler best diagnoses HSTU failures.

Practical synthesis: retain the fixed 200-user/category, 99-negative, seed-42 validation protocol as the selection criterion. Diagnose each single trained HSTU using the same users and positives across equal-sized uniform, popularity-stratified, and title/description-similar candidate sets. Report positive ranks, HR@10 changes, hit/miss disagreement, eligible-user counts, unique-negative counts, popularity-bin counts, and metadata coverage. Use paired user-level bootstrap intervals for differences; resample within categories before computing macro averages. Repeated candidate draws estimate sampling sensitivity separately from user uncertainty. These are proposed diagnostics, not established calibrated preference tests.

For the designated 20 training users, audit full-catalog unseen-item recommendations in bounded scoring chunks; report coverage, popularity exposure, and metadata redundancy descriptively. Five users/category cannot establish population-wide behavior, and without held-out targets this audit cannot measure recommendation accuracy. Unobserved items are not verified dislikes; metadata similarity can introduce false negatives. Missing exposure propensities and relevance judgments prevent claims of debiased preference measurement. Bootstrap intervals remain conditional on the fitted checkpoint and do not capture training-seed uncertainty.
